findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-SUP-014 do not define the program-code integrity method or reference value, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the program-code integrity method and reference value.

findings.description: Failure of the start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the check and its failure criterion after the program-code integrity decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 specifies segment size and frequency but not how a segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the run-time segment-check method and reference value.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time check and its failure criterion after the program-code integrity decision is made.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the precise event that triggers the latch.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the state values and their meanings.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-004 detects an unfinished execution at the limit while also permitting completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant, then make the trigger and permitted completion consistent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the complete CRC parameters, covered data range and stored-value representation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Specify the eight-report case with its applicable condition and obtain the response for zero through seven retained reports.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-030 gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify a verifiable response time or precise event for driving the signal high.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify how the service tool retrieves the reset cause.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the safe-state and recovery behavior for watchdog-reset faults.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after entering the safe state. SYS-SUP-024 requires only that transmission complete before the reset request, so it permits the report to be transmitted before safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required ordering between safe-state entry and fault-report transmission, consistent with the report deadline.
